title: Moonshot waves 1-8 at blocks 4 and 5: the 2-in-7 near miss and the shape searches
made_with: AI agents (Claude) directed by the author
notes: No finding of this section is proved in Lean; none of its proofs has been checked by a person.
Most findings were checked by one AI skeptic, not two.

findings.statement: Under the k = 8 hook at f = 9, one paid move at block 4 is worth at most 27,456 and a depth-3 piece needs 68,320; five moves allow 137,280 against 136,640 needed for two depth-3 pieces, leaving 640.
findings.status_detail: exact ranks modulo 33,554,393; reproduced by an independent AI skeptic by another method; a skeptic of a later round confirmed 68,320 is the exact value, not only a mod-p lower bound (floating-point singular values with a wide gap, two more primes on every block); 27,456 is the m = 4, k = 8 case of the hook cap formula proved in Lean (see block-bounds-and-new-rules)
findings.rerun_2026_10_19: yes: rank blocks 1,716 and 4,270 at characters 0, 1 and 7

findings.statement: No hook with k = 1 to 15 values a depth-3 piece at 2.5 moves or more; k = 7 and 9 give 2.4591, k = 6 and 10 give 2.3766; mixing hooks cannot beat k = 8.
findings.status_detail: one AI skeptic reproduced the values

findings.statement: Every free letter that relabels addresses and multiplies by phases keeps the hook test space, so making more such letters free (order-3 shifts and every other odd-order letter included) cannot change the 640; every separating end of the private-end shape asks the first five moves for exactly two depth-3 values.
findings.status_detail: one AI skeptic re-derived it and found no error

findings.statement: In the widened game the 640 rests on the guess that non-engine depth-3 targets are never cheaper at k = 8 (computed only at k = 2, 3, 4).
findings.status_detail: guess

findings.statement: The first round's hook values at odd k (k = 5, 7, 9), computed as 16 times one character block.
findings.status_detail: only valid for even k; corrected by ranking all 16 blocks (k = 7: 2.4591, not 2.476; k = 9: 2.4591, not 2.448; k = 5: 2.2552, not 2.221); the maximum stays at k = 8
findings.refuted_by: the order-3 round, which ranked all 16 character blocks; its skeptic reproduced the values

findings.statement: The closing test stated in the near-miss note (a certificate with average sin^2 below 0.7 at depth 3 closes the branch).
findings.status_detail: orbit cut 1434 has spectral factor 7/4 and s3 = 0.699 yet misses (2.483) because s1 = 858/865; the correct test is s3 < 0.7 s1
findings.refuted_by: a later certificate search and its skeptic

findings.statement: The 2-in-7 unit at block 4 with private ends (the 640 near miss).
findings.status_detail: no program found, no certificate closes it; many shapes inside it excluded (findings below)

findings.statement: With sigma the order-3 cyclic shift of three address bits, Z1 (x1 + x2) + Z2 (x1 - sigma x2) = K x1 with Z2 = K (1 - sigma + sigma^2)/2 and Z1 = Z2 sigma: two pieces separate two arrays; for an order-2 letter no such pair works.
findings.status_detail: explicit matrices at blocks 3 and 4 (an exact identity); found by the skeptic of wave 1

findings.statement: An order-3 pair at the start or the end of a program is only a change of input basis, so the order-3 halving end is a private end in other coordinates and inherits the 640.
findings.status_detail: one AI skeptic confirmed it

findings.statement: A correct 8-move program for 2 arrays at block 4 with an order-3 halving end exists; it is two private chains in the basis y = (x1 + x2, x1 - sigma x2).
findings.status_detail: exact end solve, formal identity, random complex arrays f = 1..5 (errors below 7e-16); replayed by the skeptic

findings.statement: Four shapes are dead for every choice of letters: one depth-2 carrier plus private helpers; single pieces with two-valued frustrated patterns; one depth-3 carrier for both targets; two depth-3 carriers that are not clean. A genuinely shared end for W arrays needs at least W + 1 pieces.
findings.status_detail: one AI skeptic read each proof; the first silently assumes the helper is shallower than the target

findings.statement: Sign patterns alone need four pieces to separate two arrays, so order-3 letters do better at the end.
findings.status_detail: with multi-term pieces sign letters reach three pieces for two arrays and four for three
findings.refuted_by: the skeptic of the first order-3 round (explicit examples)

findings.statement: The first order-3 searches were complete (312 template prefixes, 765 any-basis prefixes).
findings.status_detail: some end moves were never tested and one template computed nothing
findings.refuted_by: the skeptic of the first order-3 round

findings.statement: The swap-symmetric 2 in 7 at block 4 that met the frame-level test to 2.4e-10 is, normalised, a small exact program that fails the full test by a fixed amount (full residual tends to 2/3; 1 at the exact frame-level solution).
findings.status_detail: the skeptic rebuilt the closure and the tests with its own code

findings.statement: Unit/zero-divisor dilemma: in the symmetric shape with single-term shared and last moves, each array's single route 1 + a u into its target must be invertible, yet cancelling the other array's leftovers forces a = +-1, a zero divisor; so it is never a unit, for every filter, letter order and twist.
findings.status_detail: one AI skeptic upheld it and proved a stronger gadget statement; the two group-algebra facts it uses are checked by computer (programs/symmetric-2-in-7-dilemma/, re-run 19 Oct 2026)

findings.statement: Repairs of the symmetric near miss: 16 order-3 twists (residual 1.0), a junk absorber (floor 1/3), 407 + 18 twisted gadgets (fail at f = 1).
findings.status_detail: twists and absorber numerical (evidence only); gadgets computed, and the skeptic proved every gadget of that kind fails at f = 1

findings.statement: The seed-301 limit skeleton is not a unit: least f = 2 residual 0.2333 over every coefficient and limit.
findings.status_detail: numerical only (reproduced by the skeptic, 0.233327); the stated justification was wrong; evidence, not proof

findings.statement: Lemma P (separating arrays that share a generator needs frustrated signs and divides by 2) and Lemma S (two literal readings of the Fano blueprint fail for every choice of letters).
findings.status_detail: the skeptic of wave 1 checked them; Lemma P(b) needs an invertible coefficient

findings.statement: At block 4 a private last move wastes 9,184 of a move's 27,456, so 3 in 10 and 4 in 13 can end privately for at most one array and an exactly tight schedule for none.
findings.status_detail: exact ranks modulo a prime, given the counting rule; the skeptic held the arithmetic

findings.statement: The smallest frustrated set spread over frames is the Fano gadget.
findings.refuted_by: the order-3 two-piece separation found by the skeptic of wave 1

findings.statement: The Singer-cycle template (2 in 7, 3 in 10, 4 in 13 with an odd-order address relabelling separating the arrays) is excluded for every separating matrix (top rule: read backwards it has one full-length chain from the inputs, a unit needs W).
findings.status_detail: one AI skeptic re-derived it; its joint solver said yes 0 times in 2,052 calls (2 in 7) and 45 calls (3 in 10)

findings.statement: The smallest odd-order separators with support at most 3 are 1 + sigma and 1 + sigma - sigma^2, both with denominator 2.
findings.status_detail: exact enumeration

findings.statement: The block-4 engine game is exactly the dual polar graph of Sp(8,2) on 2,295 Lagrangian frames; it agrees with the real 16 x 16 matrices on 400 of 400 random words (skeptic: 1,500 of 1,500).
findings.status_detail: skeptic rebuilt it by brute force

findings.statement: Theorem A (with Lemma 5+): if u1 = D b1 y1, u2 = D b2 y2, u3 = D(r u1 + c r' u2) with single letters, in any input basis, no 4th and 5th moves deliver both depth-3 targets of a 2 in 7; engine and widened games.
findings.status_detail: one AI skeptic read every proof line by line and found no error

findings.statement: No letter advances one term of a single-letter shared move towards K while holding the other back.
findings.status_detail: Proposition S: a selective advance exists for 43,008 of 100,352 single-letter shared moves
findings.refuted_by: Proposition S, an exhaustive count in the exact model, recounted by the skeptic

findings.statement: Theorem R of shape R: with one term per frame of the third move, no 2 in 7 exists in the engine game, for every choice of letters, rational coefficients and extra terms (with Theorem Q, Lemma G, Corollary G1, Lemmas R1, R1'', R2).
findings.status_detail: one AI skeptic read every proof and rebuilt the test; 1,588 of its own prefixes, 26,869 target pairs, none passed

findings.statement: Shape-R families: 6,820 prefixes and 70,228 target pairs, none passing the exact test.
findings.status_detail: with controls; skeptic independent families agree
findings.rerun_2026_10_19: controls and families A, TYPEM: match

findings.statement: Shape R with two or more terms on a frame of the third move, and shape R in the widened game.
findings.status_detail: searched by the track and the skeptic, nothing passed, no proof

findings.statement: 1,256 of the 1,261 saved 2-in-7 prefixes at block 4 are excluded exactly over Q for every end move and every invertible free mixing of the two end moves (802 by Criterion 0, 454 by Criterion D).
findings.status_detail: the skeptic rebuilt both criteria in its own code: same verdict on all 1,261
findings.rerun_2026_10_19: Criterion 0 on all 1,261: every value matches

findings.statement: 3 of the 5 remaining prefixes are excluded against every end move within the P-test group of 24,576 letters.
findings.status_detail: exact; one decided by the skeptic

findings.statement: The last 2 saved prefixes (anyb G3S s61 #11, w3 STG2 #17) against end moves outside the pool.
findings.status_detail: their runs were left running and never collected

findings.statement: The second order-3 round's claim that 1,251 of the 1,261 prefixes were ruled out for every end move.
findings.status_detail: on 22 kframe prefixes the P-test tried only the pool end moves; corrected count 1,229 for every end move, 22 against the pool only, 10 open; superseded by finding 29

findings.statement: The 3-in-10 analogue of shape R gives dimension 0 in all 1,200 natural extensions.
findings.status_detail: one program, not repeated by anyone; no proof for three arrays

findings.statement: One shared move then two private layers (W in 3W + 1) with single-letter starts and merge: the readout of the tops is forced and a second route is only a relabelling of the top moves (Theorem R of that shape, Lemmas 1-5).
findings.status_detail: the skeptic checked the proofs line by line, twice

findings.statement: The f = 2 block test (three pieces of 16, 120, 120 dimensions; a row-space test in each) is a valid necessary test and sees the zero-divisor failure (the wave-2 near miss fails it at 0.267).
findings.status_detail: upheld by the skeptic

findings.statement: 755 small skeletons of the one-shared-move shape have no solution for any complex coefficients (Groebner basis {1} over Q in Singular).
findings.status_detail: the skeptic re-ran every decision, also modulo a prime, with its own pipeline
findings.rerun_2026_10_19: the 25 systems of the first batch regenerated byte for byte; Singular not re-run

findings.statement: The 144 one-shared-move skeletons too large to decide (133 + 11 uncounted).
findings.status_detail: a later claim to exclude 76 of them holds modulo one prime only

findings.statement: Theorem P: private starts, private layer-2 moves, one shared layer-3 move and private tops never make a unit for any W >= 2 (engine game, single letters, any injections).
findings.status_detail: one AI skeptic read it line by line and checked its geometry exhaustively over 2,295 frames (0 survivors; 1,344 with one condition dropped)

findings.statement: Shared layer-2 variant: all 68 cross cores and 34 sigma-pair cores tested are excluded at the frame level; 395 + 598 + 18 + 18 skeletons have no solution by Groebner bases; no theorem.
findings.status_detail: core verdicts upheld by the skeptic

findings.statement: Lemma D' as stated (cross form of the first-round lemma).
findings.status_detail: it misses two cancellation routes; 49,152 letters per such leftover pass a condition the proof says none can
findings.refuted_by: the skeptic of the two-shared track

findings.statement: The 99 + 9 skeletons Singular left undecided in the two-shared track are excluded too.
findings.status_detail: not confirmed: some contain two-letter injections outside the model; the skeptic job that would say which was never collected

findings.statement: The private-ending count extends to the endings with leftovers that Theorem R forces (which would close 3 in 10 and 4 in 13 in the one-shared-move shape).
findings.status_detail: argued not to extend by itself; the computation is out of reach as posed

findings.statement: Over an abelian ratio group, a rationed shared end for W arrays needs at least W fields of the rational group algebra; prime-order letters never work, order 4 works for 3 arrays only; one paid end move is never enough.
findings.status_detail: class counts checked by computer and reproduced by the skeptic; non-abelian groups not classified

findings.statement: In the coordinate world all end moves form one class.
findings.status_detail: sign letters give 4 classes, order 3 gives 2
findings.refuted_by: the skeptic of the shared-end track (coord_classes.py)

findings.statement: Shared-end searches: 1,447 prefixes for 3 in 10 and 678 for 4 in 13, none passing the relaxed level.
findings.status_detail: a numerical/sampled search found nothing; evidence, not proof

findings.statement: 7 in 23 and 8 in 26 with both shared moves first (the blueprint as written) or both last are impossible (top rule: 2 of 7 routes); F O O O F and O F O O F with single-term shared moves fail.
findings.status_detail: upheld by the skeptic; O F O O F checked exhaustively in the engine game

findings.statement: Theorem R' one step deeper: order O O F O F with a single-term middle shared move fails.
findings.status_detail: 3,024 of 286,720 configurations escaped (exhaustive); later shown spurious
findings.refuted_by: the skeptic of wave 3 (as written); then superseded

findings.statement: O O F O F with a single-term middle shared move is excluded for 7 in 23 and 8 in 26 (the read term must be exactly 2 moves from the target; 0 of 35,840 escape); 1,216 skeletons of the other orders fail; pairs of single-term shared moves serve no character (0 of 28,311,552).
findings.status_detail: one program, not repeated by anyone (the skeptic confirmed only file counts); the 7-in-23 part uses a Sylow argument, argued by hand; 520 of the 1,216 at random coefficients (screen only)

findings.statement: A 7-in-23 group-algebra program (O O F O F, middle move reading one term through 184 letters) passes the frame-level test in all 6 characters outside its own.
findings.status_detail: reproduced by the skeptic; the pass is generic (180 equations, 208 unknowns), so weak evidence

findings.statement: 8 in 26 with a group-algebra middle shared move is excluded for every twist subgroup (target outside a fixed space in at least 4 of 7 characters; at most 2 can be set aside).
findings.status_detail: the track tested 3,264 of 11,391 subgroups; the skeptic tested all 11,391 (later verdict used)

findings.statement: The 7-in-23 group-algebra construction is excluded in both orders in its configuration: O O F O F rank at most 11 where 12 is needed (constituent (14,2)); O O F F O rank at most 13 where 14 is needed once only the 4 reachable slots are free (constituent (6,5)).
findings.status_detail: exact bounds in floating point, rank gaps of 13 orders or more; not refuted: the skeptic rebuilt every space on both lifts and extended it to every pair of order-7 twists

findings.statement: An earlier round's claim that the 7-in-23 O O F O F construction was excluded.
findings.status_detail: it applied only to a generic lift; a corrected lift kept the family alive

findings.statement: 7 in 24 (O O F F O F) passes every distance-4 test computed.
findings.status_detail: top part computed, terminal move argued by hand; nothing at distance 3 or below

findings.statement: Corollary B++: in a block-5 butterfly both inputs must be injected within the first two shared moves; the ends split cleanly only for special merges.
findings.status_detail: checked by the skeptic

findings.statement: At block 5, leftovers find no partner, so the chain of cancellations stalls.
findings.status_detail: a sampling artefact
findings.refuted_by: the skeptic of wave 2 (by the exact rule every leftover at layers 3 and 4 has a partner)

findings.statement: Theorem W3: the block-5 butterfly 2 in 7 with single-letter starts, merge and trunk is never a unit, whatever the injections into the first two trunk moves, side terms into the last and end contents.
findings.status_detail: upheld by the skeptic, which redid the exact census over all 3,360 paths (0 violations over 1,720,320 pairs)

findings.statement: Several-branch trunk: Lemma P, Corollary P, Lemma L4', Lemma DC, the reduction of a split-trunk 2 in 7 to a 2 in 8, the three-middle-frames count, Lemma Q for injections into the first trunk move.
findings.status_detail: upheld by the skeptic, which proved the three-frames count and checked it over every anchor pair
findings.rerun_2026_10_19: three-frames census: rows match; the saved total line was inconsistent with its rows

findings.statement: Lemma Z' for three or more branch letters, and "a second branch in the same frame changes nothing".
findings.status_detail: escaping configurations exist (none is a unit)

findings.statement: Wave 7: Lemma E1-sigma, Lemma T (layout (4,2)/(2,4)), Corollary O.
findings.status_detail: confirmed line by line by the skeptic

findings.statement: "Only orbits that swap the branch frames can help", and the Lemma S bullet "the copy must fix array 2's target frame" in the 2-in-8.
findings.status_detail: cycle orbits help too (layer-3 residual 0.047); a two-letter start passes layers 5 and 4 exactly

findings.statement: The forced-zero closure peel.py missed forced zeros in two ways; peel2.py fixes both and audits each closure; peel.py never produced a false exclusion but kept dead designs alive.
findings.status_detail: upheld by one skeptic, which verified all 19 forced-zero chains with brute-force code

findings.statement: All 20 rebuildable layer-3 near misses of wave 7 fail layer 3 exactly (19 by forced zeros, s1302 by a rank test 168 vs 169); s801-s805 fail within two steps of the seed; s1401, s1402 fail by Groebner bases; s1404, s1503 by forced zeros; s1407-s1409 excluded.
findings.status_detail: one skeptic reproduced s1401/s1402 at a new prime and over Q and every kill chain; not re-checked: s1302 rank test, s1503, s1407-s1409
findings.rerun_2026_10_19: the 18 radius-2 systems of s801, s1401, s1402 regenerated byte for byte; solvers not re-run

findings.statement: Lemma F: in the most separated 2-in-8 layout, a far-branch column dies on its own layer-4 row unless a stream has a branch term at one prescribed frame.
findings.status_detail: no skeptic has read it

findings.statement: s1501 (2 in 8 at block 5): passes layer 4 exactly; two-step layer-3 ball consistent numerically; three-step ball fails numerically unless an injection is switched off.
findings.status_detail: layer 4 exact (skeptic); the rest numerical only
